reader.requirement: At --std 85, every numeric entry whose PICTURE has 'S' and to which no SIGN clause applies (DISPLAY, scaled with V or P, the largest 18-digit item, and the COMP/COMP-3 usages, which take no SIGN clause) carries an operational sign whose position and representation the implementor defines, here documented as DOC-A.1-177 (a fused trailing sign, `--sign-encoding` ibm by default or ascii); the compiler must apply that one documented definition consistently, and GR5 to GR7 do not bind it.
reader.edition-search: grep of Edition./CobolVersion/DialectLevel/Has( over PicInfo.cs (SignKindFor, ProfileInitializer), ZonedSign.cs and CobolNum.cs: none. EditionContext carries SignEncoding, but it is the --sign-encoding compile option (EditionContext.cs line 110-117 says it is not a dialect axis), read the same way at every --std. The path consults the edition nowhere.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness pins -123/+123 as 12L/12C, SIGN IS LEADING as J23, the width, and the valid-sign class test; not exercised: default byte-identical to SIGN IS TRAILING, zero and negative zero, V and P scaling, an 18-digit item and its size error, an unpunched digit as a positive sign, COMP-3, and the ascii encoding at 85

probes.printed: PIC S9(4) VALUE -1234 with no SIGN clause: D1X=123M, the same bytes as SIGN TRAILING (T1X=123M, DEF=TRAIL); SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE 1234-; D1 = L1 AND D1 = SP1 -> NUM-EQ; MOVE D1 TO a LEADING item -> -1234
probes.expected: the documented default: sign fused on the trailing digit, ibm characters (DOC-A.1-177); conversion between sign forms automatic
one representation for every size and scale, an operational sign kept on every value

probes.printed: X(3) "123" seen through S9(3) with no SIGN clause: IS NUMERIC true, value 0123, > 0; group G with S9(4) -5 -> [000N|]
probes.expected: the implementor's valid sign set (DOC-A.1-178) admits an unpunched digit as positive; the item adds no character position

probes.printed: --sign-encoding ascii at --std 85: D1X=123t, Z1X=000, V1X=00u, P1X=s, B18X=...y; --std 2023 (ibm) prints the same lines as --std 85
probes.expected: the documented ascii convention at 85, the same determination at every edition

probes.printed: S9(3) COMP-3 -45 and +45 seen through X(2): bytes 04 5d and 04 5c
probes.expected: the implementor's packed sign nibble (D negative, C positive); no SIGN clause may apply to COMP-3

reader.notes: SignKindFor gives an S item with no SIGN clause the TrailingOverpunch kind (BinaryMinus for COMP usages), and ZonedSign's one table pair per --sign-encoding writes it, so the default matches DOC-A.1-177 at 85 exactly as at 2023. Packed items carry the C/D sign nibble.
